title: 1994 AHSME Problem 10
statement: For distinct real numbers \(x\) and \(y,\) let \(M(x,y)\) be the larger of \(x\) and \(y\) and let \(m(x,y)\) be the smaller of \(x\) and \(y.\) If \[ a\lt b\lt c\lt d\lt e, \] then \[ \begin{aligned} &M\bigl(M(a,m(b,c)),\\ &\qquad m(d,m(a,e))\bigr)= \end{aligned} \]

solutions.text: From the ordering, \(m(b,c)=b,\) so \(M(a,m(b,c))=M(a,b)=b.\) Also \(m(a,e)=a,\) hence \(m(d,m(a,e))=m(d,a)=a.\) The outer expression is therefore \(M(b,a)=b.\) Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: The two arguments of the outermost \(M\) reduce to \(b\) and \(a\)
